rationale.conceptual: Uses SCC-DFTB, a well-documented method, with a public parameter set; no novel theory or custom algorithm; the main challenge is constructing correct initial structures and extracting properties, which is a standard application of the tool.
rationale.execution: The workflow spans 4 steps: structure construction, geometry optimization of six polymorphs, computing structural/elastic/electronic properties, and orbital analysis. It requires orchestrating DFTB+ runs, fitting an equation of state, and parsing electronic DOS. This is a moderate pipeline with several dependencies but only one external tool.

difficulty.reasoning: The paper applies an established semi-empirical method (SCC-DFTB) with a standard parameter set to a set of hypothetical BN polymorphs. The conceptual work requires understanding of solid-state physics and DFTB input but involves no custom algorithms. The execution pipeline is multi-step (structure building, multiple DFTB+ runs, post-processing) but uses a single external tool and modest I/O. Resources are minimal due to small unit cells and the CPU-only tight-binding method.

compute_estimate.reasoning: SCC-DFTB is a semi-empirical tight-binding method that runs on CPU; the largest unit cell has 32 atoms, so memory and disk usage are negligible (a few GB RAM, no large datasets).
